rules.description: Each of the last N bars closed above (long) / below (short) the prior bar's close -- a run of trending closes.

catalog_match.note: MomentumConsecutiveBars(lookback=1, consecutiveBars=trendBars-1) is exactly 'each close above the prior close, held for N consecutive bars' -- catalog's own ConsecutiveCloseExit doc confirms MomentumConsecutiveBars(lookback=1) means this. Same bars, no new rule needed.

rules.merge_notes: R00-33 (Ranges front matter, 'trending closes') and V02-24 (Reversals ch02, 'trending anything') are the same test from two chapters. On re-read this is a fixed-parameter instance of the existing catalog rule MomentumConsecutiveBars, not a new rule.

rules.description: Each of the last N bars has a body top and body bottom above (long) / below (short) those of the bar before it -- trending bodies, not just trending closes.
rules.pseudocode: forall i in 0..trendBars-1: max(open[i],close[i]) > max(open[i+1],close[i+1]) && min(open[i],close[i]) > min(open[i+1],close[i+1])
rules.merge_notes: Same book quote as TrendingCloseRun ('trending anything: closes, highs, lows, or bodies') but measures body top/bottom instead of close-to-close -- a bar can have a trending close without a trending body, so kept as its own rule per the two-behaviorally-distinct-rules test.

rules.description: Once the current pullback has retraced at least R percent of the leg's range (measured over a fixed lookback window, not a swing-pivot search), stop treating it as a with-trend pullback -- treat it as the start of a new trend in the opposite direction instead.
rules.pseudocode: legLow = lowest(low, legLookback)[1]; legHigh = highest(high, legLookback)[1]; retracement = (close[0] - legLow) / (legHigh - legLow); retracement >= retracementThreshold  // long side: reclassify a bear leg's pullback as a new bull trend; short side mirrors with legHigh/legLow swapped

complexity.reason: a fixed-window Highest/Lowest plus a ratio -- no swing-pivot search needed

rules.merge_notes: Three restatements of Brooks' '75% retracement flips trend bias' rule (Ranges Pt.III, Trends front matter, Reversals front matter). T00-22 and V00-57 define the leg's start/extreme via SwingHigh/SwingLow pivot detection; RP3-04 uses a fixed N-bar Highest/Lowest window instead, which needs no pivot machinery -- picked as the mechanizable definition per the fixed-offset-over-swing-pivot preference. Default retracementThreshold=0.75 (all three sources agree) and legLookback=30 (from RP3-04; the others leave it unstated).

rules.description: Close is at or above the highest close (long) / at or below the lowest close (short) of the N bars ending one bar ago.

catalog_match.note: Breakout is close >= highest close of the last N bars INCLUDING the current bar (a fresh window); this excludes the current bar via the [1] offset, the same exclusion convention CloseAbovePriorHighestHigh uses on highs.

rules.merge_notes: T02-14's original test ANDs this close-vs-highest-close condition with close[0] >= highest(high,N)[1], which is exactly the catalog's CloseAbovePriorHighestHigh -- dropped that AND-term as a composition of an already-catalogued rule (Atomic beats composite); this atomic close-vs-recent-closes half is what's new.

rules.description: A named Brooks setup: bars 2 and 0 form a two-bar reversal (skipping bar 1), and the skipped middle bar is small relative to recent bars. Enter beyond the combined extreme of the three bars.
rules.pseudocode: TwoBarReversal(bar2, bar0) && (high[1] - low[1]) <= middleBarMaxFraction * avgRange(rangeLookback); entry: buy stop one tick above the highest high of bars {2,1,0}

complexity.reason: reuses TwoBarReversal's ratios plus a small-middle-bar test; depends on TwoBarReversal (T06-05) being authored first

rules.merge_notes: T06-08 defines the three-bar shape (bars 2 and 0 form T06-05's two-bar reversal, skipping a small bar 1); T06-09 is its Entry order-type wrapper (stop above the three-bar combined extreme). T06-09 also describes an earlier-entry alternative when the last two bars alone already qualify as a two-bar reversal -- not mechanized here, just the standard stop-beyond-extreme entry (standing convention). Kept whole as a named Brooks setup, not split, per the composite-carrying rule for named setups (Harris-pattern precedent in the catalog).

rules.description: Over the last N bars, fewer than K closed against the intended direction -- the pullback/rally is still mostly one-sided.

catalog_match.note: TailBarCountDominance compares bull-tail vs bear-tail wick/close counts against each other; this is a single count of opposite-close bars against a fixed threshold, no wick/tail shape requirement.

rules.merge_notes: T07-39 ('block a long when >=5 of the last 6 bars closed down') and TP3-25 ('as a long filter, require the down-close count in the last 10 bars to be below 3') are the same test stated as a block-condition and an allow-condition -- allow when count < threshold is exactly not-block when count >= threshold. Defaults taken from TP3-25 (windowBars=10, maxOppositeBodies=3); T07-39's stricter (6, 5) pair recorded as an alternate parameterization.

rules.description: The instrument's recent average bar range is below a small dollar threshold -- avoid scalp-sized targets; price-action entries can still be taken but should be managed for a swing.

complexity.reason: a rolling average-range comparison against a fixed dollar threshold

catalog_match.note: AtrDollarsBelow uses the WFSafe_AvgTrueRange rolling ATR times BigPointValue against a dollar threshold; this uses a plain Average of bar range (not true range, no BigPointValue conversion) -- close in spirit but a different average and no point-value scaling, so kept as its own rule.

rules.merge_notes: Book text is stock-specific ('under a dollar'); recorded generically as minRangeDollars so it can be optimized per instrument.

rules.description: Exit the position if N consecutive bars close against it -- a tighter tolerance than a full stop, meant for positions taken on a weak original signal.
rules.pseudocode: countif(i in 0..adverseBars-1, close[i] < open[i]) == adverseBars // exit long; mirrored for shorts

complexity.reason: fixed window CountIF over bar closes

catalog_match.note: Same condition as ConsecutiveUpBars (each of the last N bars closed against its own open, mirrored) but placed in the EXIT pane -- exactly the ConsecutiveCloseExit precedent: an Entry-shaped condition needs its own Exit-role rule since an Entry cannot sit in the exit pane. Reads no position state: an exit by placement, the streak may pre-date the entry.

rules.description: The close is above the highs of at least N consecutive prior bars.

catalog_match.note: Same test: close above the highest high of the N bars ending one bar ago, EL's Highest(High,N)[1]. Already in the catalog.

rules.description: There is an elevated chance of a partial reversal or re-assessment of the day's direction around a specific clock time; use as a time gate on reversal-pattern entries.

catalog_match.note: TimeWindow(830, 930) reproduces this exactly; nothing new to author.

rules.description: Block new entries within a short window around a known scheduled-report time, when algorithmic activity dominates price action.

complexity.reason: a bar-close-time comparison against a fixed scheduled time

catalog_match.note: TimeWindow(reportTime - reportDelayMinutes, reportTime + reportDelayMinutes), negated per placement for the block sense, reproduces this exactly.

rules.description: The recent average bar range has contracted to a small fraction of its long-term average -- an extreme low-volatility state.

complexity.reason: two rolling averages compared by ratio

catalog_match.note: TrueRangeAvgRatio(lookback=shortLookback, slowFactor=longLookback/shortLookback, multiple=contractionFraction), NEGATED, reproduces this contraction test -- the catalog rule's own doc names this exact negated use as its 'volatility contraction' form.

dropped.reason: composition of catalog's HighestHighBreakout + a trivial bull-close test (close[0] > open[0]); not independently meaningful

bucket_summary: 41 keyword-leftover candidates spanning all three volumes, most of which belong to a specific existing topic bucket by content even though the keyword pass missed them; 21 are cross-bucketed (mostly to bar_anatomy_reversal_signal, breakouts_pullback_retest, support_resistance_levels, and climax_reversal, plus one -- R31-12 -- absorbed directly into trade_management since this agent owns both files). Of the 20 ids that genuinely stay in misc, three merges collapsed near-duplicate restatements (a 75%-retracement trend-reclassification filter from three sources, a body-count filter from two, and the named ThreeBarReversal pattern from two), yielding 12 rules: 6 A's (TrendingBarBodies, DeepPullbackRetracementFilter, CloseAboveHighestClose, OppositeCloseCountBelowThreshold, AverageRangeBelowDollarThreshold, AdverseBodyCountExit), 1 B (ThreeBarReversal, pending TwoBarReversal), and 5 D's that turned out to be exact catalog duplicates or fixed-parameter instances of TimeWindow/TrueRangeAvgRatio/CloseAbovePriorHighestHigh/MomentumConsecutiveBars. Three ids were dropped outright: one ad hoc composite, one superseded by the now-decided leg definition, and one blocked on unsupported multi-timeframe bar access.
